newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures finally ran out of steam late on Friday after a positive week which left the December contract near a contract high and 10-year bond yields at their lowest level since the beginning of February 1994.

Analysts said the French market remained hostage to movements in U.S. and German bond markets and there was a risk that unless U.S. data continued to point to a slowdown, bond markets could drift lower next week.
Traders said the French cash bond market felt a little heavy, with many investors reluctant to invest after the decline in yields, although there were no fears of a collapse.

"We could see some more volatility as there's a risk U.S. statistics may be heading towards a rebound in final sales which would show in the numbers at the end of the month," Valerie Plagnol, economist at Credit Commercial de France, said.

French bond futures slipped to their lows of the day after bond markets took exception to a larger-than-expected rise in U.S. consumer sentiment, which provided a good pretext for some profit-taking ahead of the weekend, traders said.
Plagnol said although fears of social and political upheaval in France had failed to materialise yet, the possibility of a political upset could explain some of France's underperformance.
The 10-year yield spread over Bunds, using the 6.50 percent 2006 OAT, moved into positive territory on Friday after a long period of outperformance by French bonds.
A cash bond trader said there had been some selling of the 10-year area on Friday following a strong performance on Thursday on the back of a couple of large orders.

He also said he remained cautious of the long end at these levels as French bond movements were largely at the mercy of movements in the U.S. and Germany. With the short end potentially vulnerable to French political shocks he said he favoured five-year bonds at the moment.

On Friday, however, a currently stable franc, coupled with hopes for a call money easing next week, kept December PIBOR in positive territory. It matched the contract high of 96.49, up three basis points, but failed to push on into new ground.
The franc traded between 3.3805 and 3.3775 per mark, ending the European session at 3.3790, unchanged from Thursday.

Plagnol said what was surprising this week was that despite a veritable barrage of comments from Bundesbank officials aimed at boosting the dollar, the mark had not weakened that much, and any further mark strength could weigh on the franc.
